report.source_text: Renal tissue histology [Figure 3] on light microscopy showed marked mesangial cell increase, some of which contain apoptotic debris; significant features of acute tubular necrosis with simplification of tubular epithelial cells, some of which are cystically dilated containing amorphous eosinophilic material; and interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy in about 10–20% of the section examined. There was no increase in the mesangial matrix and thickening or duplication of the glomerular basement membrane. Features were in keeping with lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II).

report.source_text: She underwent a series of dialysis sessions when she became oliguric and uremic during admission and received intravenous methyl prednisolone (1 g daily for 3 days) followed up with tapered doses of oral prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil (Myfortic) 720 mg bid. After 6 months of treatment, proteinuria, serum creatinine, and ESR reduced to 0.2 g/day, 94 umol/l and 44 mm/h, respectively. Her eGFR rose to 82 ml/min/1.73 m2

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old female presented with nephrotic syndrome and renal impairment, with positive ANA and elevated anti-dsDNA antibody. Renal biopsy histopathology showed mesangial proliferation and features consistent with ISN/RPS Class II lupus glomerulonephritis. Clinical course included malar rash, gum hypertrophy, bleeding, oliguria, and rising creatinine. Immunosuppressive treatment with methyl prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil led to improvement in proteinuria, creatinine, and eGFR over 6 months.
